Matrix
mā´trĭks
n. (the womb; that which first opens to birth; Hebrew rechem)
Latin matrix, womb, from mater, mother. The KJV uses it in one legal formula, all that openeth the matrix, which fixes the LORD's claim upon the firstborn.

Biblical Definition

Matrix is the KJV's word for the womb, and it appears almost exclusively in one phrase of covenant law. After the passover the command is given: “That thou shalt set apart unto the LORD all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD'S” (Exo 13:12). Its ground is the night of the tenth plague: “therefore I sacrifice to the LORD all that openeth the matrix, being males; but all the firstborn of my children I redeem” (Exo 13:15). The claim is restated without qualification: “All that openeth the matrix is mine; and every firstling among thy cattle, whether ox or sheep, that is male” (Exo 34:19). And the Levites are then taken as the substitute: “And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine” (Num 3:12). The doctrine is that the first thing a womb ever yields belongs to God by right, and that Israel keeps its firstborn sons only by redemption — a price paid, a substitute accepted.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines matrix as the womb; the cavity in which the fetus is formed and nourished; and by extension, a mould in which anything is cast or shaped.

expand to see more

MATRIX, n. The womb; the cavity in which the fetus of an animal is formed and nourished till its birth.

2. A mold; the cavity in which any thing is formed, and which gives it shape.

3. In mining, the earthy or stony substance in which metallic ores are found.

Key Scripture

Exo 13:12 — "That thou shalt set apart unto the LORD all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the LORD'S."

Exo 34:19 — "All that openeth the matrix is mine; and every firstling among thy cattle, whether ox or sheep, that is male."

Num 3:12 — "And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel instead of all the firstborn that openeth the matrix among the children of Israel: therefore the Levites shall be mine;"

Num 18:15 — "Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, which they bring unto the LORD, whether it be of men or beasts, shall be thine: nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem, and the firstling of unclean beasts shalt thou redeem."

Modern Corruption

Life in the womb is argued about as a status to be conferred, while Exodus treats the first thing a womb yields as already God's by right.

expand to see more

The formula all that openeth the matrix is mine settles a question the present age has managed to keep open. The claim in Exodus attaches at birth to what the womb yields, and it attaches by divine right rather than by human recognition — no ceremony confers it, no parent bestows it, and Israel's only option is to redeem what is already the LORD's. That is a categorically different framework from one in which value is granted to human life once it has met a threshold set by someone else.

The redemption clause is the gospel in miniature. Numbers 18:15 says that every thing that openeth the matrix shall be the priest's, and immediately adds, nevertheless the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem. The claim is not waived; it is satisfied. Israel's sons lived because a price was paid and a substitute accepted, and Luke records Mary and Joseph bringing the Lord Jesus to Jerusalem under this very law, quoting it: every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rechem (H7358), womb; the phrase peter rechem, that which openeth the womb, is the technical term for the firstborn claim.

expand to see more

Hebrew rechem (H7358) — womb, matrix; Exodus 13:12, 34:19.

Hebrew peter (H6363) — that which first opens; the firstborn of man or beast.

Hebrew bekor (H1060) — firstborn; the person the claim falls upon.

Hebrew padah (H6299) — to redeem, to ransom; the firstborn of man shalt thou surely redeem.

Hebrew qadash (H6942) — to sanctify, set apart; Exodus 13:2, sanctify unto me all the firstborn.

Usage

"“All that openeth the matrix is mine” — the claim stated without condition."

"“All the firstborn of my children I redeem” — the claim satisfied, not waived."

"“I have taken the Levites… instead of all the firstborn” — substitution written into the law."
